item.title: A Sharp Distributional Lower Bound for Planar Discrepancy
item.description: arXiv:2610.33085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the unnormalized discrepancy function of every $n$-point set in the unit square has absolute value at least $c\sqrt{1+\log n}$ on a set of measure at least $\eta$, with absolute constants $c,\eta>0$. Consequently, its $L_p$-quasinorm is bounded below by $c\,\eta^{1/p} \sqrt{1+\log n}$ for every $p>0$.
item.dc:creator: Aicke Hinrichs

item.title: On the unit group of some triquadratic fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.33110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we calculate the unit groups and the $2$-class numbers of the fields $ \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2}, \sqrt{q}, \sqrt{rs})$, where $q\equiv3\pmod4$, $r$ and $s$ are distinct prime numbers satisfying some congruent conditions. As an application of our main results, we derive the precise 2-class number for each field in our family. Furthermore, we show that Greenberg's conjecture is verified for several infinite families of real biquadratic fields.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Mahmoud Chems-Eddin, Hamza El Mamry

item.title: Two parametric $q$-supercongruences from Andrews' multi-series transformation
item.dc:creator: Liton Karmakar

item.title: On the evenness of coefficients of modular forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.33296v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the density of primes such that $a_p$ is divisible by a prime above $2$ for modular forms $f = \sum_{n \ge 1} a_n q^n$ of small levels. First, we reduce the problem to low weight and odd level, or a mod $2$ CM type form. Then, we provide calculations for the evenness of particular newforms. In particular, we provide a list of levels where this "evenness" can be computed exactly for all the forms with trivial nebentypus.
item.dc:creator: Sayantan Santra

item.title: A secondary term in the first moment of cubic $L$-functions over function fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.33505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $q$ be a fixed odd prime power with $q\equiv2\pmod3$. We study the first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet $L$-functions over $\Fq(T)$, ordered by their genus. By averaging the rational sieve variable in the double Dirichlet series of Hong and Fang, we obtain meromorphic continuation beyond the secondary polar divisor. Combining this continuation with the cubic Gauss-sum residues computed by David, Florea and Lal\'in gives an explicit term of order $q^{5g/6}$, with a real coefficient depending on $g$ modulo $6$, and an error $O_{q,\eps}(q^{(23/28+\eps)g})$. The periodic coefficient is not identically zero. The proof uses an exact first difference supplied by the functional equation, an Euler product for the sieve average, and Bochner's tube theorem in the Dirichlet variables.
item.dc:creator: Ziwei Hong

item.title: Local obstructions and certified computations for perfect powers in power sums
item.description: arXiv:2610.33567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $S_k(x)=1^k+\cdots+x^k$. We study perfect-power values of $S_k(x)$ by combining local valuations with finite congruence certificates. For an irregular Bernoulli pair $(p,r)$ with $e=v_p(B_r)\ge1$, we prove a valuation formula uniform for $k\equiv r+1\pmod{p^e(p-1)}$, subject to an explicit condition on $v_p(x(x+1))$. This gives explicit families of nonexistence results in which both $x$ and $k$ are unbounded. We also determine all solutions of $S_k(x)=y^n$ for $3\le x\le10^6$ with $x\equiv0,3\pmod4$, leaving $k$ and $n\ge2$ unrestricted and including squares. This extends Hajdu's fixed-$x$ classification in the same residue classes. A uniform restriction on the normalized odd part of $S_k(x)$ and finite certificates exclude every $k\ge6$; the remaining exponents are checked by exact integer arithmetic. The certificates admit independent verification. We further prove a limitation of congruence tests of bounded prime-power depth and solve the equation for every $x\equiv28\pmod{5\,110\,664}$.
item.dc:creator: \'Akos Pint\'er

item.title: Height growth of rational self-maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.33570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K$ be a number field or a function field of a curve. Let $f$ be a dominant rational self-map of a normal projective variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over $K$, and let $h_H\geq1$ be an ample Weil height. Let $\lambda_1(f)$ denote the first dynamical degree of $f$. We show that there is a constant $C_{f,h_H}>0$ such that, for any $n\geq1$ and any point $P\in X(\overline{K})$ with well-defined forward orbit, $h_H(f^n(P))\leq C_{f,h_H}h_H(P)n^{2(d-1)}\lambda_1(f)^n$ if $\lambda_1(f)>1$, and $h_H(f^n(P))\leq C_{f,h_H}h_H(P)n^{2d}$ if $\lambda_1(f)=1$. Over number fields, the proof combines a new uniform upper bound for arithmetic degrees with a uniform comparison of point heights. Over function fields, it relies on the corresponding uniform upper bound for geometric degrees on a projective model.
item.dc:creator: Fei Hu, Jiarui Song

item.title: Squarefree Values of Random Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.33628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we consider the error term in the expected count of squarefree values of a polynomial when evaluated at integers \(n\le N\). We prove a power saving on average over polynomials of fixed degree and height at most \(H\). Our results improve previous estimates of Browning and Shparlinski in that the required range of \(H\) is independent of the degree, but depends on \(N\)
item.dc:creator: Bryce Kerr, Watcharakiete Wongcharoenbhorn

item.title: On Lehmer's Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.33631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $m\geq 2$ be an integer, and let $d\geq 2$ be an even integer. We study monic, reciprocal, non-cyclotomic polynomials $$ P(x)=x^d+a_{d-1}x^{d-1}+\cdots+a_1x+1\in\mathbb{Z}[x]. $$ For a fixed residue class $r\in\{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}$, we prove that there exists an effectively computable constant $c_{r,m}>1$ such that the Mahler measure $$ M(P)\geq c_{r,m} $$ for every irreducible polynomial $Q$ whose inner coefficients satisfy $$ a_j\equiv r\pmod m \qquad (1\leq j\leq d-1). $$ Moreover, we explicitly compute the constant $c_{r,m}$ in terms of $r$ and $m$. For the residue classes $r=2$, $r=3$, and $r=m-1$, we obtain improved lower bounds for suitable ranges of the modulus~$m$. We also consider monic, reciprocal, irreducible, non-cyclotomic polynomials whose inner coefficients belong to two distinct residue classes modulo $m$. More precisely, if the inner coefficients with odd indices are congruent to $a\pmod m$ and those with even indices are congruent to $b\pmod m$, where $a\not\equiv b\pmod m$, then we prove the existence of a constant $c_{m,a,b}>1$ such that the Mahler measure $$ M(P)\geq c_{m,a,b}. $$ These results solve Lehmer's problem for several families of polynomials. We also construct infinitely many examples in every even degree $d\geq 2$ of monic, reciprocal, irreducible, non-cyclotomic polynomials over $\mathbb{Q}$, together with explicit information about their Mahler measures. Our proofs rely on Y. Bilu's equidistribution theorem and its effective version proved by C. D'Andrea \emph{et al.}, as well as on a method developed by P. Borwein \emph{et al.} While it is natural to consider Bilu's equidistribution results in conjunction with the Borwein {\it et al}. method to Lehmer's problem, we are not aware of any previous work in the literature that employs this particular approach.
item.dc:creator: Piyush Kumar Jha, R. Thangadurai

item.title: Zassenhaus Filtration and Ihara Constants
item.description: arXiv:2610.33649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a curve over $\mathbb{F}_q$. Denote by $N(X)$ and $g(X)$ the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points and the genus of $X$ respectively. The Ihara constant \begin{equation*} A(q)=\limsup_{g(X)\to\infty}\frac{N(X)}{g(X)} \end{equation*} measures the asymptotic abundance of rational points on curves over $\mathbb{F}_q$. In this paper, we study the Zassenhaus filtration of pro-$p$ groups arising from class field towers. By combining Golod--Shafarevich theorem, embedding problems and central class field theory, we establish a new criterion for the infinitude of class field towers. As an application, we obtain an improvement on the best known lower bounds of Ihara constant $A(2)$ and $A(3)$ which are explicitly given by \[ A(2)\geq 0.317779\cdots \text{ and } A(3)\geq 0.496074\cdots. \]
item.dc:creator: Liming Ma, Chaoping Xing, Zugan Xing

item.title: Joint Extension Field Point Counts for Superelliptic Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.33847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fix a finite field $\mathbf{F}_q$, an integer $m\ge2$ prime to $q$, and $2\le\kappa\le m$. For a uniformly chosen $\kappa$-power-free polynomial $F\in\mathbf{F}_q[x]$ of degree $D$, we determine the limiting joint distribution of the affine point counts of $y^m=F(x)$ over $\mathbf{F}_q,\ldots,\mathbf{F}_{q^n}$ as $D\to\infty$, with $q$ and $n$ fixed. The probability generating function is a finite Euler product with explicit local factors. Equivalently, the limiting vector is a sum of independent closed-point contributions, each of which may affect several extension degrees. We obtain the formula by specializing the equidistribution and motivic Euler product formalism of Bertucci-Howe. We then compute means, covariances, and moment expansions as $q$ varies in a fixed reduced residue class modulo $m$, after the degree limit has been taken. The one-field specialization recovers the power-free affine point-count distribution of Cheong-Wood-Zaman.
item.dc:creator: Yuxiang Yao, Xu Zhuang

item.title: Exploring topological features of a complex network of prime factors and composite numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.33873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prime numbers are mathematical concepts of particular interest because of their relative rarity among integers, as well as the relative unpredictability of their occurrence and density along the integer sequence. They constitute the building blocks of all other composite numbers, giving rise to the interesting and important concept of prime factorization, a process guaranteed by the fundamental theorem of arithmetic. Among the several works that have been reported about prime numbers and their interrelationship with composite numbers, some have considered derived graphs and/or networks. In this paper, we derive some topological features of a bipartite complex network of prime factors and composite numbers. More specifically, we prove mathematically that the network's diameter is exactly five regardless of the number of nodes. In particular, we show that certain nontrivial sub-networks have minimal diameter equal to four, which is, again, independent of the number of nodes as long as the network is large enough. The last shows that this network is of small-world type. We also characterize exactly the number of boundary nodes in the network and present a couple of algorithms to identify the most important, relevant, influential, or central nodes of the network. Finally, we focus on the computation of the information dimensions on the basis of Shannon and Tsallis entropies of the studied complex network. The results show both decreasing as the number of nodes increases. Furthermore, both entropies indicate that box coverings at the diameters \(\varepsilon=[3,4]\), group nodes into roughly the same number of boxes, independent of the number of nodes in the network.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Daniel Tamayo-Castro, Aldo Ramirez-Arellano, Juan Bory-Reyes

item.title: Explicit Coleman integration over finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$
item.description: arXiv:2610.33970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coleman integration is an important computational ingredient of the Chabauty--Coleman method and its extensions. We extend the Balakrishnan--Tuitman algorithm to general smooth projective curves with good reduction over arbitrary finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, allowing both ramification and nontrivial residue degree. Given a suitable plane model and integral bases, we provide explicit precision bounds and an accompanying Magma implementation. As an application, a single-prime computation at $p=19$ over the unramified quadratic extension $\mathbb{Q}_{19^2}/\mathbb{Q}_{19}$ recovers all $35$ affine sporadic quadratic divisors on $X(s3,ns5)$ over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt5)$. Completeness is proved in an appendix using symmetric Chabauty and a Mordell--Weil sieve.
item.dc:creator: Yulin Cai, Timo Keller

item.title: Finite-sum Identities and Supercongruences for Cubes of Catalan Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.34160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $C_k=\binom{2k}{k}/(k+1)$ be the $k$-th Catalan number, and let $p$ be an odd prime. We establish exact finite-sum identities that, together with known binomial supercongruences and reductions of Sun, yield $\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k^3}{16^k}\equiv2-24y^2-\frac{5p^2}{2y^2}\pmod{p^3}$ when $p=x^2+3y^2\equiv1\pmod3$, and $\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k^3}{(-8)^k}\equiv-1-48y^2-\frac{33p^2}{16y^2}\pmod{p^3}$ when $p=x^2+4y^2\equiv1\pmod4$. We also evaluate the corresponding sum with denominator $16^k(k+1)^2$, and obtain two weighted Catalan supercongruences. The finite identities follow from the ratios of consecutive summands, symmetry of double sums, and telescoping. All endpoint terms are retained over the rational numbers before any modular reduction. In each bilinear identity, one endpoint denominator equals $p$; its cancellation produces the necessary term of order $p^2$. The precise arithmetic inputs are stated separately.
item.dc:creator: Yuqi Liu

item.title: Cross numbers and the characterization of finite abelian groups by length sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.34288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Characterization Problem asks whether a finite abelian group with Davenport constant at least four is determined, up to isomorphism, by its system of length sets. This is a central inverse problem in non-unique factorization theory: it asks whether the possible numbers of irreducible factors retain enough information to recover the underlying class group. For rings of integers of algebraic number fields, an affirmative answer means that the ideal class group can be recovered from these factorization lengths alone. We resolve this problem for all homocyclic groups $C_n^r$: if $G$ is a finite abelian group with $\mathsf D(G)\ge4$ and $\mathcal L(G)=\mathcal L(C_n^r)$, then $G\cong C_n^r$. The cross number of a sequence is the sum of the reciprocals of the orders of its terms. This weighted measure of sequence length links zero-sum theory with half-factoriality, and determining its maximal value for minimal zero-sum sequences is a longstanding extremal problem. We also obtain an exact formula for the maximal cross number of minimal zero-sum sequences over subsets whose minimum distance is divisible by the rank of the ambient group minus one. For $G\cong C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_r}$ with $1<n_1\mid\cdots\mid n_r$ and $r\ge\max\{2,n_r-2\}$, we prove \[ \mathsf K(G,r-1)=1+(r-1)\sum_{p\mid n_1} \left(1-p^{-\mathsf v_p(n_1)}\right), \] which is a key ingredient in resolving the Characterization Problem for homocyclic groups.
item.dc:creator: Qinghai Zhong

item.title: Three Quadratic Recurrences Modulo 3: What We Can Prove and What We Can Guess
item.description: arXiv:2610.34300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study three innocent-looking recurrences modulo $3$, each built from squares of two earlier terms. One of them turns out to be secretly $\textit{linear}$, and we can compute its periods exactly. One is a $\textit{permutation}$ hiding a small, perfectly orderly piece inside a large, random-looking one. The third looks thoroughly random, but it still has a few provable features. Along the way we meet open problems that need nothing beyond a first course in abstract algebra to state. This paper is a starting point, not the final word in any sense.
item.dc:creator: Steven Finch

item.title: On real biquadratic number fields for which the $2$-Iwasawa module has rank $3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.34400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the stability of the $2$-rank in the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_2$-extension of real biquadratic number fields. We determine several families of real biquadratic fields $F$ for which the ranks of the $2$-class group $A(F)$ and the associated $2$-Iwasawa module $A_\infty(F)$ are both equal to $3$. More precisely, we provide a complete classification of all fields $F=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{q},\sqrt{d}),$ where $q\equiv 3\pmod{4}$ is a prime number and $d$ is an odd positive square-free integer, and all fields $F=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2q},\sqrt{d}),$ where $q\equiv 3\pmod{4}$ is a prime number and $d\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ is a positive square-free integer, for which $ \operatorname{rank}(A(F))=\operatorname{rank}(A_\infty(F))=3.$
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Mahmoud Chems-Eddin, Ikrame Daqaq

item.title: A symmetric extension of Zhao's series for $\zeta(5)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.34482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a four-parameter extension of Zhao's series for $\zeta(5)$. Restricting a Wilf-Zeilberger seed of Au to a hyperplane, we obtain a summand in five parameters with zero sum that is symmetric under all their permutations. Summing it from two different starting points gives two trigonometric closed forms, which we prove by Guillera's periodicity argument. The proof is self-contained, and also gives a companion series for $1/\pi^2$, which we have not found in the literature. Specializing the parameters at roots of unity, we obtain Borwein-Bradley-type identities whose products depend only on $x^2$, $x^3$, $x^4$ or $x^5$. Their Taylor coefficients are Ap\'ery-like series for odd zeta values and for products of zeta values. In particular, we prove five identities conjectured by Au.
item.dc:creator: Noam Shalev

item.title: Frangible prime gaps
item.description: arXiv:2610.34525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A prime gap $(p_n, p_{n+1})$ is \textit{frangible} if the smallest prime divisor of every integer $m$ with $p_n<m<p_{n+1}$ is strictly less than the size of the gap, $p_{n+1}-p_n$. Gafni and Tao recently proved that the number of frangible gaps up to $X$ is $\ll X/\log^2 X$, answering a question of Erd\H{o}s. They also showed that under the Dickson--Hardy--Littlewood prime tuples conjecture this number is $\sim c X/\log^2 X$ for a constant $c$, for which they obtained a rough estimate. We describe improved methods for estimating this constant under the same hypothesis, and establish that its value lies in $[2.7416, 2.7984]$, confirming a speculation of Gafni and Tao. In addition, we present the results of a complete survey of frangible gaps up to $10^{17}$. An ensuing empirical measurement of $c$ matches our estimate very well.
item.dc:creator: Michael J. Mossinghoff, Timothy S. Trudgian

item.title: Results for distinct covering systems with a prime minimum modulus $q \ge 11$
item.description: arXiv:2610.34541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that if the smallest modulus of a covering system is a prime $q \ge 11$, then the sum of the reciprocals of the moduli is at least $1+10^{-28}$. This improves on a previous more general bound of the first two authors in this particular case. We also show that it is impossible to construct a covering system using distinct multiples of $q$ as moduli. Finally, we show as a corollary that it is impossible to construct $10$ distinct covering systems with the property that no modulus is used in more than one of the covering systems.
item.dc:creator: Michael Filaseta, Alexandros Kalogirou, Jonah Klein

item.title: Admissible sets of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1
item.description: arXiv:2610.34556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal O_K$ be the ring of integers of a number field $K$. A finite subset $\mathcal H=\{\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_k\}\subset\mathcal O_K$ is said to be \emph{admissible} if for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ in $\mathcal O_K$, the reductions of the $\eta_i$ modulo $\mathfrak p$ do not represent every residue class. The diameter of a finite subset $S$ of $\mathcal O_K$ is defined to be \[\mathrm{diam}(S):= \max_{\eta_i,\eta_j\in S:\eta_i\neq\eta_j}|\mathcal N(\eta_i-\eta_j)|\] where $\mathcal N$ denotes the norm down to the rational field. This paper computationally investigates admissible subsets of rings of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1 (such as the Gaussian integers or the Eisenstein integers) that are large relative to their diameter. The motivation is twofold. Firstly, there is the improvement of results analogous to the question of an upper bound for the least gap between large rational primes, which has been one of the great number theoretic successes of the twenty-first century. A second motivation is that there is the opportunity to disprove a variation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture. The calculations in the paper provide new records on the smallest distance between primes in the fields in question, and explicit counter-examples to a generalisation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture in all bar one of the fields.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Shiu

item.title: Finiteness theorems for trace Euclidean quadratic lattices over totally real number fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.34604v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by Clark's work on Euclidean quadratic forms, we introduce trace Euclidean and house Euclidean quadratic lattices over totally real number fields, and relate these concepts through the $p$-norm Euclidean property. We prove that, as $F$ varies over all totally real number fields of arbitrary degree, there are only finitely many positive definite trace Euclidean $\mathcal{O}_{F}$-lattices of arbitrary rank $n\ge1$, up to isometry. For every $p\in[1,\infty]$, the same finiteness holds for positive definite $p$-norm Euclidean lattices. We also classify all positive definite trace Euclidean lattices of rank one over real quadratic fields: there are exactly six isometry classes, and every such lattice is free. As a corollary, the trace Euclidean real quadratic fields are precisely $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2})$, $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$, and $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{13})$.
item.dc:creator: Zilong He

item.title: Geometric progressions in distance sets in odd dimensions over prime fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.34758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $E\subset\mathbb{F}_p^d$, let $\Delta(E)=\{Q_d(x-y):x,y\in E\}$, where $Q_d(z)=z_1^2+\cdots+z_d^2$. We introduce and study the problem of the existence of nondegenerate three-term geometric progressions in the distance set $\Delta(E)$ when $d$ is odd. If $M_{GP,d}(p)$ denotes the largest size of a set whose distance set contains no such progression, then, for every prime $p\geq7$ and every integer $m\geq0$, \[ p^mM_{GP,1}(p)\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq4p^mM_{GP,1}(p). \] For all sufficiently large primes $p$, we also prove \[ p^{m+\frac{7}{26}}\leq M_{GP,2m+1}(p) \leq Cp^{m+\frac{16}{25}}, \] where $C$ is an absolute positive constant.
item.dc:creator: Thang Pham, Dung The Tran, Boqing Xue

item.title: The Family $X_{qp^s}$ for Distinct Primes $q,p$ in Connection with Carmichael's Totient Conjecture
item.description:
arXiv:2610.34808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shannon, Shiue, Saito and the author \cite{SSHS2025} studied the sets $X_k=\{n\in\mathbb{N}:\varphi(n)=k\}$ in connection with Carmichael's totient conjecture, and proved that for an odd prime $p
eq3$ and $s\in\{1,2,3,4\}$, $X_{2p^s}$ is empty whenever $2p^s+1$ is not prime (with $s=1$ fully characterized in both directions), conjecturing that this persists for every $s\ge1$. We resolve that conjecture in full, obtaining a complete characterization of $X_{2p^s}$ for every $s\ge1$ and every odd prime $p
eq3$, together with a parity dichotomy: $X_{2p^s}=\varnothing$ unconditionally whenever $s$ is even, while for odd $s$ both outcomes genuinely occur, determined exactly by the primality of $2p^s+1$. We then close the one remaining gap at $p=3$, where the proof technique degenerates, with a separate, unconditional characterization of $X_{2\cdot3^s}$. Building on these results, we consider the natural generalization $X_{qp^s}$, where $q
eq p$ are distinct primes and $s\ge1$. We show that this generalization splits into three cases of very different character. If $q$ and $p$ are both odd, the problem is trivial: $qp^s$ is odd, so $X_{qp^s}=\varnothing$ by elementary parity, with no case-analysis needed. If $q=2$, the problem is exactly the family $X_{2p^s}$ resolved above. If $p=2$, giving the ``mirror'' family $X_{2^sq}$ for an odd prime $q$, the problem is genuinely different. Beyond $s=1$, we give a complete resolution for $s=2$, recovering, with an explicit proof and solution sets, the qualitative dichotomy of \cite[Thm.~2.3.1]{SSHS2025}, but the problem remains open for $s\ge3$.
item.dc:creator: Tian-Xiao He

item.title: Hartl's dictionary and a transcendence characterization of equicharacteristic local shtukas with complex multiplication
item.description: arXiv:2610.34822v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We update Hartl's dictionary between $p$-adic Hodge theory and its equicharacteristic analog to include aspects related to the Hodge--Tate filtration in $p$-adic Hodge theory and its equicharacteristic analog, the Hodge--Tate--Taguchi filtration. Using this update, we establish a transcendence characterization of equicharacteristic local shtukas with abelian Tannakian structure group, matching a result of Howe--Klevdal in the $p$-adic setting. A special case of this result says that a formal Drinfeld module over an equicharacteristic local field has complex multiplication if and only if the Hodge--Tate--Taguchi filtration on its $z$-adic Tate module is algebraic.
item.dc:creator: Minhua Cheng, Sean Howe

item.title: Dynamical Chowla conjecture for polynomials of several variables
item.description: arXiv:2610.34912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1965, Chowla conjectured that the mean value of the Liouville function at non-square one-variable polynomials is zero. This conjecture is a generalization of the prime number theorem (PNT). In 2022, Bergelson and Richter established a dynamical generalization of this form of the PNT. For non-square multivariate polynomials, one also expects that Chowla's conjecture is true. In this article, we extend Bergelson and Richter's result to multivariate polynomials whose Birch rank is sufficiently large in terms of their degree. We also establish analogous results for averages over integer points on algebraic varieties.
item.dc:creator: Biao Wang, Daodao Yang

item.title: Counting Integral Matrices with Given Cubic Characteristic Polynomial
item.description: arXiv:2610.34973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the number of $3\times 3$ matrices with given characteristic polynomial and entries in $\mathbb{Z}\cap [-H,H]$ is at most $c H^{3}(\log H)^{6}$ for all $H\ge 2$, where $c>0$ is an absolute constant.
item.dc:creator: Philipp Habegger

item.title: Non-liftability of the field of norms of the $p$-adic false Tate curve extension
item.description: arXiv:2610.35006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p\geq3$ be a prime number. We prove that the action of the Galois group on the field of norms of the $p$-adic false Tate curve extension $\mathbf{Q}_p\left(\zeta_{p^\infty},p^{1/p^\infty}\right)$ of $\mathbf{Q}_p$ is not liftable to its Cohen ring with respect to any admissible coefficient field.
item.dc:creator: Yijun Yuan

item.title: On almost perfect additive complements
item.description: arXiv:2610.35027v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $A, B$ be infinite sets of non-negative integers with $n\in A+B$ for all sufficiently large integers $n$. We prove that if $A(x)B(x)-x$ does not tend to infinity, then $$\limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}\in\Big[\frac{3}{2}, 2\Big].$$ The lower bound is sharp, and confirms a conjecture of Chen. Our proof is based on the weak limits and the convolution factorization theorem of Gabardo and Lai. A discrete proof of the same bound was also given by Zhang. Motivated by the known spectrum of perfect additive complements, we conjecture that the interval $(3/2, 8/5)$ is also excluded for almost perfect additive complements.
item.dc:creator: Wouter van Doorn, Boning Liu, Quanyu Tang

item.title: Galois groups of polynomials over a fixed number field: determinant methods in general boxes, resolvents, and quantitative counting
item.description: arXiv:2610.35030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K$ be a fixed number field of degree $d$. We prove two determinant-method results for integral points over $\mathcal O_K$ in boxes whose coordinates may have different size bounds: a Bombieri-Pila type estimate for affine plane curves that retains the two separate coordinate bounds, and a Salberger-Browning covering theorem for affine surfaces. If $F\in\mathcal O_K[X_1,X_2]$ is irreducible and $T=\max B_1^{e_1}B_2^{e_2}$ over the monomials occurring in $F$, then \[ N_K(F;B_1,B_2)\ll T^\varepsilon \exp\!\left(d\frac{\log B_1\log B_2}{\log T}\right). \] For an absolutely irreducible surface in three variables we obtain a covering by $O(T^\varepsilon V_{3,K})$ bounded-degree auxiliary hypersurfaces, outside $O(T^\varepsilon V_{3,K}^2)$ exceptional integral points, where \[ V_{3,K}=\exp\!\left(d \left(\frac{\log B_1\log B_2\log B_3}{\log T}\right)^{1/2}\right). \] These are the number-field analogues of determinant-method estimates for unequal coordinate ranges developed in the rational setting by Browning and Heath-Brown, Salberger, Browning, and Chow-Dietmann. We then apply them to Galois resolvents of monic degree-$n$ polynomials over $K$. Independently, a large-sieve argument, in the tradition of Gallagher's probabilistic Galois theory, gives $O_{K,n}(N^{dn-d/2}\log N)$ exceptional separable polynomials, while effective Hilbert irreducibility over global fields gives subgroup-sensitive bounds with exponent $d(n-1+1/[S_n:G])$, up to logarithms. We record the interaction with the discriminant-square equation for even groups, congruence restrictions, and rectangular coefficient boxes. All determinant estimates used in the applications are proved in the paper; no conjectural global-field determinant statement is assumed.
item.dc:creator: Ilaria Viglino

item.title: Weighted density bounds for covering systems over Dedekind domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.35139v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the density of uncovered sets arising from finite families of residue classes over Dedekind domains with finite residue norms. Building on the distortion method of Balister, Bollob\'as, Morris, Sahasrabudhe and Tiba, we prove a general weighted density criterion in which the weight attached to a prime ideal is allowed to vary. In the critical Mertens regime this yields, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), the admissible prime-ideal weight \[ 1+\frac{(\log N\mathfrak p)^3(\log\log N\mathfrak p)^{1+\varepsilon}}{N\mathfrak p}, \] up to a harmless modification at finitely many small prime ideals. This is asymptotically smaller than the fixed weight \(1+(\log N\mathfrak p)^{3+\varepsilon}/N\mathfrak p\) appearing in the earlier density theorem. The result is valid for systems of any fixed multiplicity and, for multiplicity one, requires the ideal moduli themselves to be distinct but not their norms. We then place the analytic hypotheses in Knopfmacher's Axiom~A framework. In the critical case of Axiom~A with exponent \(1\), the prime-ideal estimates needed by the weighted theorem are automatic. More generally, under Axiom~A with exponent \(\rho>0\), we prove a weighted mean-value theorem on ideals; in the subcritical range \(0<\rho<1\), a first-moment argument shows that sufficiently large moduli cover an arbitrarily small proportion of the ambient space. We also explain that the distortion construction itself only uses a compatible system of finite residue spaces with uniform fibres and a Chinese-remainder-type product structure, suggesting a possible extension beyond Dedekind domains. Finally, we show that a direct passage from the second moment to higher integer moments does not lower the logarithmic exponent \(3\) within this moment hierarchy.
item.dc:creator: Jihui Chen

item.title: Bounds on the number of squares in recurrence sequences: $y_{0}=b^{2}$ (II)
item.description: arXiv:2610.35158v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For binary recurrence sequences, $\left( y_{k} \right)_{k \in \bbZ}$, arising from the solutions of generalised Pell equations, $X^{2}-dY^{2}=c$, where $y_{0}$ is any positive square and $c=-2^{\ell}p^{m}$ for an odd prime $p$ and non-negative integers $\ell$ and $m$, we show that there are at most $4$ distinct squares with $y_{k}$ sufficiently large. From this result, we also show that there are at most $7$ distinct squares when $y_{0}=1,2^{2},\ldots,7^{2}$, or once $d$ exceeds an explicit lower bound, without any conditions on the size of such squares.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Research in Number Theory, volume 12, article 6 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Paul M Voutier

item.title: Congruences modulo powers of $7$ for partitions with colored odd parts
item.description: arXiv:2610.35292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $a_k(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ in which even parts occur in one color and odd parts may occur in $k$ colors. We prove infinite families of congruences modulo powers of $7$ for $a_k(n)$ when $k \in \{4,5,7\}$. For each positive integer $\alpha$, let $\lambda_{k,\alpha}$ be the least nonnegative solution of $24\lambda_{k,\alpha}\equiv-(k-2)\pmod{7^\alpha}$. Then, we show that \[ a_k(7^\alpha n+\lambda_{k,\alpha}) \equiv 0\pmod{7^{\lfloor(\alpha+1)/2\rfloor}} \] for every nonnegative integer $n$. These results extend congruences modulo $7$ of Hirschhorn and Sellers (2026) and complement Chen's (2025) congruences for the reciprocal crank parity function $a_3(n)$.
item.dc:creator: Saikat Maity, Manjil P. Saikia, Prabal Talukdar

item.title: Spectral zeta functions in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2610.35306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spectral zeta functions and zeta-regularized determinants encode the spectrum of an operator in analytic functions. Over the completion $\mathbb C_\infty$ of an algebraic closure of $\mathbb F_q((\pi))$, two features of characteristic $p$ break this classical picture. Complex powers have exponents that vary only continuously in $\mathbb Z_p$, not analytically. Scalar traces record eigenvalue multiplicities only modulo $p$. We develop a resolvent-based theory that treats these two obstructions separately. For the first, inverse Stieltjes duality turns suitable scalar resolvents into locally analytic spectral distributions on $\mathbb F_q[[\pi]]$. A single exponent of the Mellin transform already determines the distribution and the entire Mellin family. We characterize exactly which power series arise in this way, by a growth condition on Carlitz moments. The criterion depends on the support: bounded Taylor coefficients are not sufficient. For stationary digit measures, the transform is the unique fixed point of an explicit contraction. The first $q-1$ nonconstant moments recover the measure. For the second, we replace traces by the Frobenius defect $F/\sigma(F)$, where $\sigma$ raises coefficients to their $q$th powers. On power series with small coefficients, this map is a group automorphism that preserves Gauss distances, and a convergent infinite product inverts it. Polynomial defects produce entire functions. They characterize exactly the diagonal spectra that are finite unions of forward Frobenius orbits, counted with multiplicity. For the shifted Carlitz operator, the resulting Fredholm determinant is a normalized reciprocal of the Anderson--Thakur function, and its Newton polygon is determined exactly.
item.dc:creator: Su Hu, Min-Soo Kim

item.title: On Hecke algebras at exceptional Eisenstein primes
item.description: arXiv:2610.35559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the structure over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ of the Hecke algebra acting on ordinary cusp forms in the Eisenstein, non-$p$-distinguished case. Our results and methods draw on four complementary approaches: deformation theory, through $R=\mathbf{T}$ theorems; Iwasawa theory, through connections to Sharifi's conjecture; $p$-adic $L$-functions, through an exceptional zero formula; and computational experiments using Magma. We also obtain new results regarding the Coleman--Greenberg conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Maksoud

item.title: On the Hasse principle for a block-diagonal form and a form of lower degree
item.description: arXiv:2610.35639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the Hasse principle for systems consisting of one form of degree $k$ which decomposes as a sum of $n$-ary forms, and one general form of degree $d < k$. By exploiting the block structure of the first form before applying Weyl differencing, we refine the method of Brandes and Parsell (arXiv:2003.04350) in this setting; in particular, for a sum of binary quartic forms and a quadratic form, the requirement $s > 516$ is relaxed to $s > 96$, which also improves on the bound $s > 100$ available for general forms.
item.dc:creator: Anna Theorin Johansson

item.title: On explicit formulas for Grassmannian polylogarithms and Gelfand-MacPherson forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.35754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We answer a question of Goncharov by showing that his Grassmannian $n$-logarithm can be recovered by integrating the Borel invariant form on the symmetric space $\mathrm{SL}_{n}(\mathbf{C})/\mathrm{SU}(n)$ over a naturally defined ideal simplex. As corollaries, we recover the finiteness of primitive canonical integrals of Brown and the evaluation for wheel graphs of Brown and Schnetz. We also compute explicitly the Gelfand-MacPherson forms for powers of the first Pontryagin class and give a general integral formula for the Gelfand-MacPherson forms associated to each component of the Pontryagin character.
item.dc:creator: Juan Diego Rojas

item.title: Improved lattice-packing bounds in small dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.35830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We strengthen the upper bound on the density of a lattice packing in small dimensions. A lattice cannot have too many short vectors; we modify the Cohn--Elkies linear program accordingly by allowing the auxiliary function to be positive on a short interval beyond the minimum distance. For $11 \leq n \leq 16$, our bound is tighter than the three-point bound of Cohn, de Laat and Salmon. For $n \in [17, 23] \cup [25, 40] \cup [43, 57] \cup [62, 75]\cup [83, 91]$, our bound lies below the published numerical values of the Cohn--Elkies bound.
item.dc:creator: Nina Zubrilina

item.title: On the magic positivity of the Ehrhart polynomials of dilated base polytope of minimal matroid
item.description: arXiv:2610.32050v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we consider the magic positivity of the Ehrhart polynomial of dilated base polytope of minimal matroid of rank $k$ dimension $n$. We prove that for $\displaystyle 1\leq k<\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor$, the $n-k-1$ dilate of the Ehrhart polynomial is not magic positive. We also show that for sufficiently large $n$, the $n-k$ dilate of the Ehrhart polynomial is, in general, magic positive. This gives rise to a lower bound of the $m-$index of the Ehrhart polynomial.
item.dc:creator: Jiaxuan Chen, Chance Crigler, Shengtao Ding, Dana Paquin, Julian Schennach

item.title: Stability of certain elements in the Bernstein center
item.description: arXiv:2610.33327v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a split connected reductive algebraic group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. The stable center conjecture asserts that the subspace of stable elements in the Bernstein center of $G(F)$ is a sub-algebra, and this subring is conjecturally isomorphic to the regular functions on the moduli of semi-simple Langlands parameters. Bezrukavnikov-Kazhdan-Varshavsky suggested an approach towards the stable center conjecture by explicitly constructing elements and proving their stability directly without assuming LLC, and proved the stability of the depth-$r$ projectors. Following the idea, the first author and Tsao-Hsien Chen produced a family of elements in the center which are conjecturally stable using Deligne-Lusztig parameters attached to irreducible representations. This paper proves the stability of the projectors corresponding to strongly regular Deligne-Lusztig parameters in depth-zero, and for all the positive depth elements with some restrictions on the residue characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Sarbartha Bhattacharya, Shenghao Li

item.title: Brauer--Manin obstruction for Weil restrictions
item.description: arXiv:2610.33736v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a quasi-projective variety $X$ defined over a number field $k$, let $X'$ be its Weil restriction with respect to a finite field extension $k/k'$. We prove that the Brauer--Manin set of $X$ agrees with the Brauer--Manin set of $X'$. We also prove the agreement for Brauer--Manin set of them given by $\mathrm{Br}_1$.
item.dc:creator: Hui Zhang

item.title: Inequalities and asymptotics for hook numbers in two partition functions of MacMahon and Andrews
item.description: arXiv:2610.33791v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by recent studies of hook length biases in restricted partitions, we investigate the total number of hooks of fixed length in two partition functions introduced by MacMahon and Andrews. In $1916$, MacMahon proved that the number of partitions of $n$ in which no part appears with multiplicity one equals the number of partitions of $n$ into parts that are even or congruent to $3 \pmod{6}$. For a positive integer $r$, let $A_r(n)$ count the partitions of $n$ in which every part occurring an odd number of times occurs at least $2r+1$ times, and let $B_r(n)$ count the partitions into parts that are even or congruent to $2r+1 \pmod{4r+2}$. Andrews proved that $A_r(n)=B_r(n)$ for all positive integers $r$ and nonnegative integers $n$, thereby recovering MacMahon's identity as the special case $r=1$. We derive generating functions and asymptotic formulas for the total numbers of hooks of lengths $1$, $2$, and $3$ in both partition classes, employing Wright's circle method. These asymptotic formulas yield several hook length bias results. In particular, for sufficiently large $n$, the $B_r$-type partitions exhibit more $1$-hooks than the $A_r$-type partitions, whereas for hook lengths $2$ and $3$, the bias is reversed when $r=1$ and favors the $B_r$-type partitions when $r\geq 2$. We also establish asymptotic inequalities among hook numbers of different lengths within each partition class. Finally, for fixed hook lengths $\ell\in\{1,2,3\}$, we prove that the $B_r$-type partitions exhibit more $\ell$-hooks than the $B_{r+1}$-type partitions for sufficiently large $n$. These results reveal systematic asymptotic patterns in the distribution of small hook lengths across the two partition families.
item.dc:creator: Rupam Barman, Archit Deb, Sayantan Ghorai

item.title: Fine points of the moduli space of cubic rational maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.33990v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A rational point of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_3$ of cubic rational maps is fine if its conjugacy class contains a map defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, and coarse otherwise. In the invariants $\xi_0,\dots,\xi_5$ that embed $\mathcal{M}_3$ in $\mathbb{P}(2,2,3,3,4,6)$, we prove that a point with trivial automorphism group is fine if and only if the quaternion algebra $(-m_{12},-2\xi_0)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ splits, where $m_{12}=\frac{1}{3}\xi_0^2\xi_1+\xi_0\xi_4-\xi_3^2$; we give the analogous criterion on the locus $\mathcal{L}_2$ of maps with an involution and show that all other strata are fine. The proof is constructive and yields an explicit descent. We prove that the obstruction class is unramified along every divisor of the compactification, that a prime $p\ge 5$ obstructs only if the point reduces modulo $p$ into the closure of one of the two codimension-two loci $\mathcal{L}_1$, $\mathcal{L}_2$ of maps with an involution, and that $\mathcal{M}_3$ has transverse $A_1$-singularities along both, above which the class ramifies; local densities predict that $\mathcal{L}_2$ is met modulo $p$ with probability $\asymp 1/p$, so that it carries the obstruction. A census of all 214,260,288 rational points of weighted moduli height at most 7 agrees with this mechanism and supports the conjecture that the proportion of fine points tends to zero like $(\log B)^{-1/2}$.
item.dc:creator: Tanush Shaska

item.title: MDS codes containing a fixed subcode over finite field extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.34016v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $2\le k\le n$ and let $U\le\mathbb{F}_q^n$ be a fixed $(k-1)$-dimensional linear code. We study the $[n,k]$ maximum distance separable (MDS) codes over finite extensions of $\mathbb{F}_q$ that contain the scalar extension of $U$. Our approach constructs an auxiliary linear code from \(U\). Its full-weight words characterize the desired MDS completions. We prove that \(U\) admits an \([n,k]\) MDS completion over some finite extension of \(\mathbb{F}_q\) if and only if \(d(U)\ge n-k+1\). When this condition holds, the number of these MDS codes over $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$ is \[\#\left\{W\le\mathbb{F}_{q^m}^n:U\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q}\mathbb{F}_{q^m}\subseteq W,\ \dim_{\mathbb{F}_{q^m}} W=k,\ W\text{ is MDS}\right\}=\frac{\chi_{\delta_GM(G)}(q^m)}{q^m-1},\] where $G$ is a generator matrix of $U$, $\delta_GM(G)$ is its represented derived matroid, and $\chi_{\delta_GM(G)}$ is its characteristic polynomial. In particular, the formula determines existence over each extension field and the least extension degree for which such an MDS code exists. Examples show that these counts may distinguish different representations of the same column matroid, while monomially inequivalent codes may have identical counts over every finite extension.
item.dc:creator: Yangcheng Li, Pingzhi Yuan

item.title: On the Torsion Subgroup of the N\'eron--Severi Group
item.description: arXiv:2610.34115v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove an explicit bound for the torsion subgroup of the N\'eron--Severi group of a smooth projective complex variety. The proof combines the Diophantine-approximation method of Ziyang Gao and the author (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22285) with Lefschetz fibrations. As an application, we deduce an explicit bound for the torsion sections of a traceless abelian scheme over a complex curve.
item.dc:creator: Kaiyuan Gu

item.title: Colored Partitions and Minimal Excludants
item.description: arXiv:2610.34155v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this article, we introduce the concept of minimal excludants in colored partitions and extend it to the framework of least $r$-gaps. In particular, we focus on $k$-colored partitions and cubic partitions, deriving the generating functions for the sums of minimal excludants and least $r$-gaps, and analyzing their asymptotic behaviors. Notably, the presented theory is comprehensively extended by the systematic generalization of each result for minimal excludants in $k$-colored partitions to the case of least $r$-gaps. We introduce generalized cubic partitions and discover the minimal excludant, as well as several additional results.
item.dc:creator: Suverchla Arora, Meenakshi Rana, Shruti Sharma, Nilanjan Bag

item.title: Temporal central limit theorem for mixed-radix odometer discrepancy
item.description: arXiv:2610.34243v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the local discrepancy for the number of visits of the orbit of $0$ under a mixed-radix odometer to intervals near the origin. Both the length of the orbit and the endpoint of the visited interval are chosen independently and uniformly at random. Under a Feller-type condition and an explicit condition ensuring that the finite random-time clock can be approximated by a Haar clock on the fluctuation scale, we obtain a temporal central limit theorem for the discrepancy, with an explicit Kolmogorov-Smirnov rate of convergence. This extends and strengthens the fixed-base temporal central limit theorem of Levin and Merzbach to the mixed-radix setting.
item.dc:creator: Maria Avdeeva, Francesco Cellarosi

item.title: Pointwise ergodic theorems along oscillating sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.34301v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish the first pointwise convergence result for nonconventional ergodic averages modeled along a large class of oscillating sequences, treating, for example, orbits of the form $\big(\lfloor n^d\sin(e\pi n)\rfloor\big)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$, $d\in\mathbb{N}$. More specifically, for every probability space $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ equipped with an invertible measure-preserving transformation $T\colon X\to X$ and every $f\in L^p_{\mu}(X)$ with $p\in(1,\infty]$, we prove that the limit \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^Nf\big(T^{\lfloor P(n)\psi(\alpha n)\rfloor}x\big)\quad\text{exists for $\mu$-a.e. $x\in X$,} \] where $P$ is a non-constant polynomial with real coefficients, $\psi$ is $1$-periodic and real-analytic, and $\alpha$ has irrationality exponent smaller than $1+\sqrt{\operatorname{deg}(P)+1}$. On the one hand, the latter assumption is satisfied by a.e. $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, and, on the other hand, our result covers any of the following concrete orbits \[ \lfloor n\cos(e\pi n)\rfloor\text{,}\quad\lfloor n^{37}\sin(n)\rfloor\text{,}\quad\big\lfloor \sqrt{2}n^{10}e^{\sin(\pi (\sqrt[5]{7}+1) n)}\big\rfloor\text{,}\quad \big\lfloor \big((\log 2) n^3+e n\big)e^{e^{\cos(\pi \sqrt{2} n)}}\big\rfloor\text{.} \] The proof employs the so-called one-frequency circle method for estimating exponential sums with phases $\big(\xi \lfloor P(n)\psi(\alpha n)\rfloor\big)_{1\le n\le N}$, but the major arc approximants of our exponential sums do not consist of their direct continuous counterparts. In the major arc regime we decouple the $\psi$-oscillatory part of the phase from the polynomial one, and approximate the exponential sum by $\int_0^1\big(\frac{1}{N}\int_0^Ne^{2\pi i\xi P(t)\psi( s)}dt\big)ds$. This represents a novel phenomenon for problems of this kind, and, interestingly, our proof exploits the coefficient-free variational estimates of Radon-type operators.
item.dc:creator: Leonidas Daskalakis

item.title: Uniqueness of the maximal function field with the third largest genus in characteristic $3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.35241v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $n$ be a positive integer and define $q=3^n$. It is well known that there exists a maximal function field $Z_3$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ of genus $g_3=q(q-1)/6$ and that $g_3$ is the third largest genus a maximal function field over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ can have. In this article we show that any maximal function field over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ of genus $g_3$ is isomorphic to $Z_3$. This extends previously known uniqueness result for the largest and second largest genera of maximal curves.
item.dc:creator: Peter Beelen, Maria Montanucci, Jonathan Niemann

item.title: Modular Existential Closedness
item.description: arXiv:2610.35409v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the Modular Existential Closedness conjecture for the modular $j$-function extended from the upper half-plane to $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$ by Schwarz reflection. Specifically, we show that any system of equations involving the field operations and $j$ has solutions in the complex numbers unless it is overdetermined. Such a system is overdetermined if, roughly, there are more independent equations than variables, possibly after applying the transformation rules of the $j$-function under the linear fractional action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Q})$ on $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. In general, we do not expect overdetermined systems of equations to have solutions due to the algebraic and transcendental properties of the $j$-function captured by the modular analogue of Schanuel's conjecture. In geometric terms, Modular Existential Closedness states that given a broad and free irreducible algebraic variety $V \subseteq \mathbb{C}^n \times \mathbb{C}^n$ -- where broadness and freeness are geometric conditions guaranteeing that the system is not overdetermined -- there is a point of the form $(\tau_1, \ldots, \tau_n, j(\tau_1), \ldots, j(\tau_n)) \in V$ with $\tau_i \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. The proof uses Ratner's theorems on the closure and equidistribution of the orbits of unipotent flows in powers of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ to describe the asymptotic behaviour of the orbits of certain analytic maps. This is then applied to approximate a relatively simple system of equations using the original system and the action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$. The construction of the limiting system makes use of the Ax--Schanuel theorem and guarantees an isolated solution. Rouch\'e's theorem then establishes the existence of solutions for the original system of equations.
item.dc:creator: Vahagn Aslanyan

item.title: Proofs of strong forms of the Bovdi--Geche universality conjecture and a complex analogue
item.description: arXiv:2610.35645v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove two universality theorems for neural networks consisting of a single neuron. First we prove a strong form of the Bovdi--Geche universality conjecture on neurons over finite fields, where the activation function is a certain modification of the discrete logarithm, using the Weil bound on multiplicative character sums over finite fields. Then we show a generalisation of Aizenberg's universality theorem for complex binary neurons with a weight vector independent of the target function, positively answering another question in the literature. The proof of the latter uses an equidistribution theorem for the dilates of certain maps into tori.
item.dc:creator: Victor Bovdi, Ambrus Pal

item.title: Characterising canonical lifts of ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.35807v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Brantner-Taelman's canonical lifts of ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties and characterise their (quasi)canonical lifts in terms of rational $p$-adic Hodge theoretic data. We also show that these canonical lifts need not be of CM type and that the associated local Galois representations need not split as sums of twists of unramified representations, in contrast to classical results for abelian varieties and K3 surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Samuel A. Moore

item.title: Properties C and D fail for $C_n^r$ whenever $n \equiv 2 \bmod 4, n\geq 6$ and $r\geq 4$
item.description: arXiv:2610.35819v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $s(C_n^r)$ be the Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv constant (zero-sums of length exactly $n$) and $\eta(C_n^r)$ the short zero-sum constant. Properties C and D of Gao et al.\ assert that every sequence of the extremal length without the relevant zero-sums has the form $T^{n-1}$. For even $n$ they imply $s(C_n^r)=2^r(n-1)+1$ and $\eta(C_n^r)=(2^r-1)(n-1)+1$. G.~Wang recently disproved both for $C_6^r$, $r\ge4$. We prove that both fail for $C_n^r$ for every $n\equiv2\pmod4$ with $n\ge6$ and every $r\ge4$. More precisely, for these $n$ we have: $s(C_n^r)\ge2^r(n-1)+2^{r-2}+1$.
item.dc:creator: Christian Elsholtz

item.title: Arbitrarily Many Primitive Prime Divisors in an Iterate of $x^d+c$
item.description: arXiv:2209.07624v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers $R$, let $f_{d,c}(x)=x^d+c\in K[x]$ be a unicritical polynomial of degree $d\ge2$, and let $\varrho_d(n,c)$ denote the number of primitive prime divisors of $f_{d,c}^n(0)$, the $n$-th term of the critical orbit of $f_{d,c}$. We show that $\varrho_d(n,c)$ admits no uniform bound, that is, no bound depending only on $d$ and $n$. More precisely, for all $n\ge1$ and $t\ge1$ there is $c\in R$ for which $f_{d,c}^n(0)$ has at least $t$ primitive prime divisors, and these primes may be prescribed to occur with any given multiplicities. This can be done simultaneously for any finite set of iterates. The construction rests on a density computation. Namely, the set of primes occurring as a primitive prime divisor of $f_{d,c}^n(0)$ for some $c$ has positive density. We compute that density explicitly for $d=2$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, under a hypothesis on the Galois group of the associated Gleason polynomial, verified for $n\le16$. As an application, we produce, for every $m\ge1$, a parameter $c\in R$ (in fact, a whole residue class of them), for which the splitting field of $f_{d,c}^m(x)$ has the maximal possible degree over $K$.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Sadek, Mohamed Wafik

item.title: On the mean square gap between primes
item.description: arXiv:2212.10867v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the average size of the squares of differences between consecutive primes less than $x$ is $O(x^{0.23+\varepsilon})$ for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$. This improves on a result of Peck, who gave bound $O(x^{0.25+\varepsilon})$ in the place of $O(x^{0.23+\varepsilon})$. Key ingredients are Harman's sieve, Heath-Brown's mean value theorem for sparse Dirichlet polynomials and Heath-Brown's $R^*$ bound.
item.dc:creator: Julia Stadlmann

item.title: Large sieve inequalities with power moduli and Waring's problem
item.description: arXiv:2303.07613v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We improve the large sieve inequality with $k$th-power moduli, for all $k\ge 4$. Our method relates these inequalities to a restricted variant of Waring's problem. Firstly, we input a classical divisor bound on the number of representations of a positive integer as a sum of two $k$th-powers. Secondly, we input a recent and general result of Wooley on mean values of exponential sums. Lastly, we state a conditional result, based on the conjectural Hardy-Littlewood formula for the number of representations of a large positive integer as a sum of $k+1$ $k$th-powers.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Baier, Sean B. Lynch

item.title: Bushnell-Reiner zeta functions over two-dimensional semilocal rings
item.description: arXiv:2310.15545v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Lustig gave an infinite product formula for the zeta function of a commutative two-dimensional regular local ring with finite residue field. We extend this to the noncommutative setting with a method based on filtration by an invertible ideal. One application gives an abstract two-dimensional analogue of Hey's formula. Another application provides effective formulae for zeta functions over Rump's two-dimensional regular semiperfect rings. In the appendices, we supplement these two-dimensional applications with requisite one-dimensional calculations.
item.dc:creator: Sean B. Lynch

item.title: On group rings of the simple group of order 168, 504 or 360 and their modules
item.description: arXiv:2502.20800v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and $\mathbb{Z}_p$ the ring of $p$-adic integers. Let $G$ denote the simple group of order 168, 504 or 360. In this paper, we study the structure of the $\chi$-part of a $\mathbb{Z}_p[\mathrm{Im}(\chi)][G]$-module come from ideal class groups, Artin $L$-functions and Iwasawa theory. After this manuscript was posted, it was pointed out to the author that the main theorem holds for an arbitrary finite group and follows directly from the structure theorem for group rings; see the note added after Theorem 1.1.
item.dc:creator: Yutaka Konomi

item.title: Equidistribution of integers represented by standard quadratic form under arithmetic constraints
item.description: arXiv:2503.03873v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the equidistribution of integers of the form $n= x_1^2 + \cdots + x_d^2$ under the arithmetic constraints given by $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^d$. The first step in addressing this problem is to construct modular forms whose Fourier expansion coefficients correspond to the counting problem over the quadric in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ induced by the standard quadratic form, subject to the aforementioned arithmetic constraints. The weak modular property of these modular forms allows us to use representation theory to identify the congruence subgroup to which our modular forms correspond. We then establish a necessary and sufficient condition for functions on $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^d$ that defines a cusp form. Finally, we conclude that the equidistribution phenomenon occurs locally on $p+1$ orbits for $d \geq 4$.
item.dc:creator: Yefei Ma

item.title: Differential operators on Hermitian modular forms on $\mathrm{U}(n, n)$
item.description: arXiv:2506.18236v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct explicit differential operators on hermitian modular forms, extending methods developed for Siegel modular forms. These differential operators are closely related to the two-variable spherical pluriharmonic polynomials. We construct explicit bases for the space of such polynomials and use them to build concrete operators. As an application, we derive an exact pullback formula for hermitian Eisenstein series.
item.dc:creator: Nobuki Takeda

item.title: Analogues of Traverso's Isogeny Conjecture for Some Unitary p-Divisible Groups
item.description: arXiv:2507.19708v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and $\Bbbk$ an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$. Two invariants worthy of study for a $p$-divisible group $X$ over $\Bbbk$ are its isogeny cutoff $b_X$, which measures the amount of $p$-torsion necessary to determine the Newton polygon of $X$, and its minimal height $q_X$, which measures its distance to the closest minimal $p$-divisible group (in the sense of Oort). Traverso's Isogeny Conjecture predicts a bound on $b_X$ in terms of its height and dimension. The conjecture was proved in [NV07] and a refinement was given in [LNV13]; the latter also gives a bound on $q_X$. In this paper, we study these invariants when restricting to the class of supersingular unitary $p$-divisible groups $X$ of signature $(a,g-a)$, where $0 < a < g$, for $p > 2$, and prove further refinements on their bounds purely in terms of $a$. In particular, we provide a complete description of the possible values of $q_X$. Finally, we rephrase our results in the language of the $\mathrm{BT}_m$ stratifications of characteristic-$p$ fibers of Shimura varieties for $\mathrm{GU}(a, g-a)$ in the case of an inert prime $p > 2$.
item.dc:creator: Emerald Andrews, Deewang Bhamidipati, Maria Fox, Heidi Goodson, Steven R. Groen, Sandra Nair

item.title: The $\rho$-Fourier transform
item.description: arXiv:2512.00182v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a reductive group over a local field $F$ and let $\rho:{}^LG \to \mathrm{GL}_{V_{\rho}}(\mathbb{C})$ be a representation of its $L$-group satisfying suitable assumptions. Braverman, Kazhdan and Ng\^o conjectured that one has a $\rho$-Fourier transform satisfying certain desiderata. We give a uniform construction of the Fourier transform for arbitrary local fields. This complements work of L.~Lafforgue in the non-Archimedean case, and proves a portion of the conjectures of Braverman, Kazhdan and Ng\^o. Our methods are spectral in nature.
item.dc:creator: Jayce R. Getz, Armando Guti\'errez Terradillos, Farid Hosseinijafari, Aaron Slipper, Guodong Xi, HaoYun Yao, Alan Zhao

item.title: The Hasse principle for diagonal forms restricted to a hypersurface of adjacent degree
item.description: arXiv:2601.18581v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the Hasse principle for Diophantine systems consisting of one diagonal form of degree $k$ and one general form of degree $k-1$. By refining the method of Brandes and Parsell (arXiv:2003.04350) in this specific setting, we improve the bound $n > 2^k k$ to $n > 2^{k-1}(2k-1)$; in particular, the requirement $n > 24$ in the case of degrees three and two is relaxed to $n > 20$.
item.dc:creator: Anna Theorin Johansson

item.title: Lubin's conjecture for height-one $p$-adic dynamical systems over $p(p-1)$-tame extensions
item.description: arXiv:2603.03873v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove Lubin's conjecture for height-one commuting pairs of formal power series defined over the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}$ of finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ whose ramification index is coprime to $p(p-1)$. For such a pair $(f, u)$, with $f$ noninvertible and $u$ invertible, we show that $(f, u)$ is a pair of endomorphisms of a formal group defined over $\mathcal{O}$. The proof relies on extracting a crystalline character of weight $1$ from the Galois set $T_f$ of $f$-consistent sequences, using it to define a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module structure on $T_f$ for which $f$ is an endomorphism, and applying explicit functors in integral $p$-adic Hodge theory to recover the latent formal group.
item.dc:creator: Martin Debaisieux

item.title: Analytic Study of $p$-Bessel Functions: Fractional Calculus, Integral Representations, and Complex Extensions
item.description: arXiv:2603.21072v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a systematic analytic study of the $p$-Bessel functions $\mathcal{J}_{\omega,\varphi}^{[p]}$, a novel class of generalized Bessel functions arising from Fourier analysis on planar domains bounded by $p$-circles, including astroid-type shapes with $0<p\le2$ satisfying $(2/p)\in\mathbb{N}$. While previous work established Hardy-type oscillatory identities for these domains, expressing lattice point discrepancies via $p$-Bessel functions, the present paper focuses on the intrinsic analytic properties of the functions themselves. In particular, we (i) construct a hierarchical structure of $\{\mathcal{J}_{\omega,\varphi}^{[p]}\}_{\omega\ge0}$ using Erd\'{e}lyi-Kober-type fractional derivatives, (ii) derive explicit real-analytic integral representations and obtain asymptotic formulas on the coordinate axes, and (iii) extend the functions to the complex domain through Poisson-type integral formulas. These results establish $p$-Bessel functions as genuinely new oscillatory kernels, providing a rigorous framework for studying anisotropic oscillatory phenomena and laying the analytic foundation for applications in $p$-circle lattice point problems.
item.dc:creator: Masaya Kitajima

item.title: Second order Recurrences, quadratic number fields and cyclic codes
item.description: arXiv:2603.25343v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Wall-Sun-Sun primes (shortly WSS primes) are defined as those primes $p$ such that the period of the Fibonacci recurrence is the same modulo $p$ and modulo $p^2.$ This concept has been generalized recently to certain second order recurrences whose characteristic polynomials admit as a zero the principal unit of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d}),$ for some integer $d>0.$ Primes of the latter type we call $WSS(d).$ They correspond to the case when $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d})$ is not $p$-rational. For such a prime $p$ we study the weight distributions of the cyclic codes over $\mathbb{F}_p$ and $\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$ whose check polynomial is the reciprocal of the said characteristic polynomial. Some of these codes are MDS (reducible case) or NMDS (irreducible case).
item.dc:creator: Minjia Shi, Xuan Wang, Bouazzaoui Zakariae, Jon-Lark Kim, Patrick Sol\'e

item.title: Explicit Kodaira-Spencer maps over PEL Shimura varieties
item.description: arXiv:2604.17792v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The goal of our work is to construct a class of morphisms between two canonical line bundles on integral models of PEL Shimura varieties via Kodaira--Spencer maps, and explicitly compute such morphisms and their effects on the canonical metrics of line bundles. This result provides a concrete method for comparing two canonical line bundles and the corresponding arithmetic intersection numbers. In particular, it allows us to give an explicit relationship between the height functions defined by these two line bundles.
item.dc:creator: Ziqi Guo

item.title: Consecutive non-square non-primitive pairs in a finite field
item.description: arXiv:2604.21429v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $q$ be an odd prime power and write \[ \theta_q := \frac{\phi(q-1)}{q-1}. \] If $\theta_q < \tfrac{1}{3}$, or if $\theta_q = \tfrac{1}{3}$ and $q \notin \{7,13,19,25,37\}$, then the finite field $\F$ contains a pair of consecutive elements that are both non-square and non-primitive. This extends a result of Jarso and Trudgian for prime fields $\Fp$, where the same conclusion was obtained under the stronger condition $\theta_p \le \tfrac{1}{4}$. More generally, let $\ell$ be the least odd prime divisor of $q-1$. If $\theta_q \le \tfrac{1}{3}$, then $\F$ contains a pair of consecutive elements that are non-squares and $\ell$th powers, with the sole exceptions $q \in \{7,13,19,25,37,43\}$.
item.dc:creator: Stephen D. Cohen

item.title: On optimization on ravine functions. Minkowski-Cohn moduli surface in Cohn parameterization
item.description: arXiv:2604.23871v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper presents a brief overview of ravine functions using the example of the Minkowski-Cohn moduli surface from the point of view of optimization on it. Elements of representation and solution of the minimization problem at a point are presented.
item.dc:creator: Nikolaj M. Glazunov

item.title: On the Face Map of the Admissible Set With Parahoric Level
item.description: arXiv:2605.15657v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To each face $\mathcal{F}$ of the coweight polytope $\mathcal{P}_{\mu}$, we associate a subset $\text{Adm}(\mu)_{\mathcal{F}}$ of the $\mu$-admissible set $\text{Adm}(\mu)$, which we refer to as a face of $\text{Adm}(\mu)$. This gives rise to a face decomposition of $\text{Adm}(\mu)$. As an application, we give a complete description of the fibers of the face map $|\Delta|^f$ defined by Pappas-Rapoport and prove that the face map is surjective.
item.dc:creator: Qingchao Yu

item.title: Iwasawa invariants of sharp/flat $2$-adic $L$-functions for quadratic twists of elliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2607.05305v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The aim of this paper is to study the variation under quadratic twists of the analytic Iwasawa invariants of Sprung's sharp/flat 2-adic $L$-functions for elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with good supersingular reduction at $2$. Under the hypothesis that the $\mu$-invariant vanishes, we obtain an explicit formula for the sharp/flat $\lambda$-invariants. This formula gives a supersingular analogue of Matsuno's formula in the good ordinary case. As an application, we show that the sharp/flat $\lambda$-invariants can be made arbitrarily large even among quadratic twists by single primes. Moreover, using the method of Hatley-Ray, we obtain an asymptotic lower bound for the number of quadratic twists with a prescribed sharp/flat 2-adic Iwasawa $\lambda$-invariant.
item.dc:creator: Taiga Adachi

item.title: A sharp almost sure upper bound for partial sums of random multiplicative functions
item.description: arXiv:2607.29429v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that, for either a Steinhaus random multiplicative function or a Rademacher random multiplicative function $f$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, almost surely $|\sum_{n\le x}f(n)|\ll_{\varepsilon,f}\sqrt{x}(\log\log x)^{1/4+\varepsilon}$. Together with Harper's almost sure lower bound, this determines the sharp logarithmic exponent in both models. This settles Harper's conjecture on the large fluctuations of random multiplicative functions.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Durkan, Andrew Pearce-Crump

item.title: Rigidity of Averages over the Two Largest Prime Factors
item.description: arXiv:2608.05191v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $P_1(n)$ and $P_2(n)$ be the largest and second-largest distinct prime factors of $n$. Alladi and Johnson asked whether there is a bounded function $f$ on the primes such that the averages $\frac{1}{x}\sum_{2\le n\le x}f(P_1(n))$ and $\frac{1}{x}\sum_{2\le n\le x}f(P_2(n))$ converge to different limits, where $f(P_2(n))=0$ when $n$ is a prime power. We show that this cannot happen. In fact, whenever the first average converges, the second also converges to the same limit.
item.dc:creator: Dijia Chen

item.title: Two averaged dynamical generalizations of Chowla's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2608.16108v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $k\ge1$ be an integer and let $\lambda$ be the Liouville function. In 1965, Chowla gave a conjecture that the values of $\lambda(n+h_1),\dots, \lambda(n+h_k)$ are asymptotically unrelated for any distinct natural numbers $h_1, \dots, h_k$. In this article, motivated by the recent work of Bergelson and Richter on the dynamical generalizations of the prime number theorem, we will show a dynamical generalization of Chowla's conjecture on average. In the proof, we follow an approach of Qi and Zheng who established a variant of Bergelson and Richter's theorem over irreducible binary cubic forms. Moreover, we will use this approach to show an analogue of the dynamical Chowla's conjecture along the primes on average. In 2016, Tao proved that the two-point logarithmic Chowla's conjecture holds. Recently, Charamaras and Richter generalized Tao's theorem to bounded arithmetic functions and proposed a conjecture that generalizes Chowla's conjecture to bounded multi-variable arithmetic functions. Building on their work, we prove a dynamical generalization of Tao's theorem and a variant for the composition of the sum-of-digits function with the prime Omega function.
item.dc:creator: Biao Wang

item.title: Discrete dynamics of Eratosthenes sieve
item.description: arXiv:2608.26384v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Eratosthenes sieve as a discrete dynamic system. At each stage of the sieve there is a cycle of gaps ${\mathcal G}(p^\#)$ of length $\phi(p^\#)$ and span $p^\#$. There is a recursion ${\mathcal G}(p_k^\#)\longrightarrow {\mathcal G}(p_{k+1}^\#)$ that creates the next cycle from the current one. If we take initial conditions from the cycle ${\mathcal G}(p_0^\#)$, then for all constellations of span $|s| < 2p_1$, including gaps $g < 2p_1$, the driving terms of various lengths form Markov chains. These yield {\em exact} models for the populations $n_s(p_k^\#)$ for all further stages of the sieve. If $s$ is an admissible constellation of length $J$, then its population $n_{s,J}(p^\#)$ grows as $\Theta \left( \prod (q-J-1)\right)$. So we factor out the superexponential growth to obtain the exact model for the relative population $w_s(p_k^\#)$ of the constellation $s$ across all further stages of the sieve. $$ w_{s,J}(p_k^\#) \; = \; n_{s,J}(p_k^\#) \, / \, \prod_{J+1 < p \le p_k} (p-J-1) $$ The asymptotic value of the relative population is a constant ${w_{s,J}(\infty) \ge 1}$ that depends only on the odd prime factors that divide a span in $s$. Assuming that the instances of a constellation $s$ are approximately uniformly distributed in ${\mathcal G}(p_k^\#)$, we develop initial estimates of the number of instances $s$ that would occur in the interval of survival $\Delta H(p_k) = (p_k^2, p_{k+1}^2)$. We define a statistic $\eta_s(p_k)$, the quadratic density of the constellation $s$ over the interval $\Delta H(p_k)$. We show that the initial estimates $\widehat{\eta_g}(p)$ for prime gaps agree with samples up to $5.677\,E14$.
item.dc:creator: Fred B. Holt

item.title: Central non-vanishing of Dirichlet $L$-functions
item.description: arXiv:2609.06167v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that, for every sufficiently large modulus $q\not\equiv2\bmod4$, at least $3/8-o(1)$ of the primitive Dirichlet characters $\chi$ modulo $q$ have $L(1/2,\chi)\ne0$. We also establish stronger proportions for moduli $q$ satisfying certain arithmetic conditions.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Durkan, Andrew Pearce-Crump

item.title: Internal congruences modulo powers of 2 for $k$-colored overpartitions into odd parts
item.description: arXiv:2609.11806v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\overline{po}_k(n)$ denote the number of $k$-colored overpartitions of $n$ into odd parts. For every odd number of colors, we establish infinite families of internal congruences modulo high powers of $2$. The proof proceeds by expressing the relevant difference generating functions as a fixed theta quotient multiplied by polynomials in an auxiliary function. Uniform lower bounds for the $2$-adic valuations of the polynomial coefficients then yield the stated internal congruences. These results generalize an internal congruence of Saikia, Sarma and Sellers (J. Ramanujan Math. Soc.~2025) on overpartition triples into odd parts.
item.dc:creator: Manjil P. Saikia, Prabal Talukdar, Dazhao Tang

item.title: Averaged dynamical generalizations of Chowla's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.14492v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1965, Chowla conjectured that the signs of the Liouville function become asymptotically uncorrelated at any fixed collection of distinct shifts. In 2015, Matom\"aki, Radziwi\l\l and Tao proved an averaged form of Chowla's conjecture. In 2022, Lichtman proved a variant of this conjecture over primes on average. In the same year, Lichtman and Ter\"av\"ainen proved the Hardy-Littlewood-Chowla conjecture on average. In this article, motivated by the recent work of Bergelson and Richter on the dynamical generalizations of the prime number theorem, we will first establish the analogous dynamical generalizations of these three results related to Chowla's conjecture. In the proofs, we follow an approach of Qi and Zheng who established a variant of Bergelson and Richter's theorem over irreducible binary cubic forms. In 2016, Tao proved that the two-point logarithmic Chowla's conjecture holds. Recently, Charamaras and Richter generalized Tao's theorem to bounded arithmetic functions and proposed a conjecture that generalizes Chowla's conjecture to bounded multi-variable arithmetic functions. Building on their work, we will also prove a dynamical generalization of Tao's theorem and some variants for the composition of the sum-of-digits function with the prime Omega function.
item.dc:creator: Biao Wang, Shaoyun Yi

item.title: On the arithmetic of Tate-Shafarevich groups via Kolyvagin's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.15328v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate how Heegner points detect the finiteness of the $p$-primary part of Tate-Shafarevich groups of semi-stable elliptic curves over the rationals of \emph{arbitrary} rank with any good reduction prime $p \geq 5$ with irreducible mod $p$ representation and partially recover \c{C}iperiani--Wiles' theorem on solvable points on genus one curves. As a key ingredient of the proof of these results, we also give a concise proof of Kolyvagin's conjecture for semi-stable elliptic curves with supersingular reduction with a relevant choice of an imaginary quadratic field. Our approach is independent of the cyclotomic Iwasawa main conjecture for elliptic curves with supersingular reduction.
item.dc:creator: Chan-Ho Kim

item.title: Graded Algebras of Modular Forms and Sign Changes of Fourier Coefficients for Eta Quotients
item.description: arXiv:2609.18339v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, for $N=8,12,16,20,32$, we determine the explicit structure of the graded algebra of modular forms for $\varGamma_0(N)$ of both integral and half-integral weights, with all quadratic Dirichlet characters modulo $N$. We give explicit eta quotient generators and determine the relations among them. Using these structures, for a given weight, a level among those considered above, and a quadratic character, we obtain a basis for the corresponding space of modular forms consisting of eta quotients.
