Using these eta quotient bases, we obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for the periodicity of the signs of the Fourier coefficients of modular forms in three specific spaces. Finally, we determine all eta quotients in these spaces whose Fourier coefficient signs are periodic.
item.dc:creator: Jianwen Gan

item.title: An improvement of the large sieve for square moduli under Hooley's hypothesis $R^*$ for short Sali\'e sums
item.description: arXiv:2609.21195v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $S(Q,M,N,(a_n))=\sum_{q\le Q}\sum_{a\bmod q^2,(a,q)=1}|\sum_{M<n\le M+N}a_ne(an/q^2)|^2$ be Zhao's large sieve sum with square moduli. Zhao conjectured that $S\ll(QN)^\epsilon(Q^3+N)\sum|a_n|^2$. The bound of Baier and Zhao (2008) exceeds this conjecture by a factor which reaches $Q^{1/2}$ at the critical point $N=Q^3$, and there the exponent $1/2$ has not been lowered since. We prove that, under Hooley's Hypothesis $R^*$ for short Sali\'e sums, $S\ll(QN)^\epsilon(Q^3+N+Q^{4/3}N^{2/3})\sum|a_n|^2$. This replaces the excess over Zhao's conjecture by its $2/3$-th power throughout the range $Q^{5/2}<N<Q^4$; at $N=Q^3$ it gives $S\ll Q^{1/2-1/6+\epsilon}N\sum|a_n|^2$. The proof is short. Following Zhao's original treatment, we approximate the point under consideration by fractions $b/r$ with denominators up to $Q^{2/3}N^{1/3}$, which for $N<Q^4$ is beyond the customary $\sqrt{N}$. If the approximation is poor, an elementary count suffices. If it is good, the analytic part of the problem disappears: after Poisson summation in both variables the count is expressed through quadratic Gauss sums, and their exact evaluation at every modulus turns the sum over the dual variable into short Kloosterman and Sali\'e sums, to which Hypothesis $R^*$ applies and gives the square root of the elementary count. At odd moduli the hypothesis is needed only in the form of Conjecture (C*) of Friedlander and Iwaniec. The Gauss-sum evaluations, including even moduli and coefficients sharing a factor with the modulus, are proved in full. This version supersedes earlier versions, which obtained the exponent $1/2-1/28$ at $N=Q^3$ by a much longer route through sums of modular square roots. The paper was prepared in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic).
item.dc:creator: Stephan Baier

item.title: Lower Bounds for Localised Moments of Automorphic L-functions
item.description: arXiv:2609.32673v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we describe a method to obtain lower bounds for the $2k$th moment of values of $L$-functions localised at the central point for all real $k > 0$. In particular, for the families of quadratic twists of self-dual irreducible unitary cuspidal automorphic representations of $\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$ and $\operatorname{GL}_3(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$ our results are new in the range $0<k<\tfrac12$.
item.dc:creator: Deep Thakur

item.title: Some arithmetical aspects of the two dimensional Jacobian Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.02961v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that any counter-example to the two dimensional Jacobian Conjecture with integral coefficients and determinant of its Jacobian matrix equals one, has only paths of asymptotic values that can contain only finitely many points of the planar integral lattice. The second part of our paper gives some nontrivial applications of the theory of certain Theta functions to the two dimensional Jacobian Conjecture over the real field, and over the complex field.
item.dc:creator: Ronen Peretz

item.title: Ideal Classes of Order $2^n$ in a Family of Totally Real Cubic Fields and Rational Points on Associated Elliptic Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.04254v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every prime $\ell\geq5$ and integer $n\geq2$, we construct a totally real cubic field in the family studied by Ennola with a specified prime ideal above $\ell$ whose class has exact order $2^n$. For parameters satisfying two square conditions and explicit congruences, the same squareclass obstructions give four independent rational points on the associated elliptic curves. A Pell equation describes all such parameters. A genus-one base change gives five independent sections that generate a subgroup saturated at two. It also yields infinitely many elliptic curves over $\mathbb Q$, pairwise nonisomorphic over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$, with rank at least five.
item.dc:creator: Junyu Lu

item.title: Intersecting a curve in an abelian variety with multiples of another curve
item.description: arXiv:2610.10212v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Levin asked what can be said about the locus of points lying on a given curve in $\mathbb{G}_m^n$ that have a non-zero integer power on another given curve in $\mathbb{G}_m^n$ for $n \geq 3$. We give a definite answer to the abelian analog of Levin's question, proving what is predicted by the Zilber-Pink conjecture in this case. An important ingredient in our proof is a strengthening of a height inequality by Vojta and R\'emond.
item.dc:creator: Fabrizio Barroero, Gabriel A. Dill, Lars Kuehne

item.title: Non-vanishing of primitive cubic, quartic and sextic L-functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15316v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish lower bounds for the non-vanishing proportions of primitive cubic, quartic and sextic Dirichlet $L$-functions over $\F_q[T]$ in the non-Kummer setting. Adapting truncated-exponential techniques for shifted moments, we improve the cubic lower bound of David, Florea and Lal\'in and obtain positive lower bounds for quartic and sextic families. For each family, the lower limit of the non-vanishing proportion exceeds $e^{-e^{53}}$ as the conductor degree tends to infinity with $q$ fixed. We use a common choice of truncation parameters and explicitly control the exceptional sets. The cubic argument uses the published twisted first moment. We also establish uniform twisted first moments in the quartic and sextic cases, yielding an asymptotic formula for the sextic first moment.
item.dc:creator: Ziwei Hong

item.title: Pointwise improvement of the error term in the higher rank hyperbolic lattice counting problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.16668v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove an upper bound for the error term in the higher rank hyperbolic lattice counting problem for ${\hbox{SL}(n, \mathbb{Z})}$. Blomer and Lutsko achieved recently a significant improvement of previous known results by Duke--Rudnick--Sarnak and Gorodnik--Nevo--Yehoshua. We deduce an improved upper bound for the error which holds for almost all pairs $z,w \in {\hbox{SL}(n, \mathbb{R})}$. We also derive a $\Omega$-result for the error term, in the spirit of Phillips--Rudnick.
item.dc:creator: Dimitrios Chatzakos, Panagiotis Dimakis, Christos Katsivelos

item.title: A Half-Constant Upper Bound for Chowla's Cosine Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.17160v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let lambda(n) denote the infimum of -min_x sum_{a in A} cos(ax) over all sets A of n positive integers. While the classical Sidon-difference construction yields lambda(n) <= (1 + o(1))sqrt(n)/2, we construct sets achieving a leading constant of 1/2: lambda(n) <= (1/2)sqrt(n) + O(n^(1/4)sqrt(log n)), establishing limsup_{n->infinity} lambda(n)/sqrt(n) <= 1/2. This construction combines a two-sided Sidon square identity, a Singer difference set, a Fejer-kernel majorant, a parity-biased deletion, and an exact-cardinality probabilistic selection. We also provide an L^4 criterion and a multiplicity bound constraining any construction with a smaller leading constant. In the opposite direction, we incorporate the L^1 norm into Bedert's boundary estimate with an explicit constant, yielding two lower bounds for f_A(x) = sum_{a in A} cos(ax): (1) -min f_A >= cn^(1/4) for every n-element set A subset of [1, Cn]; and (2) (-min f_A)^3 ||f_A||_1^2 >= cn for every n-element set A subset of N. The second bound recovers the 1/5 exponent of Bedert and Shankar and improves it whenever ||f_A||_1 is small relative to -min f_A. Numerical values of the construction are reported up to |A| = 25,440.
item.dc:creator: Bryan Bu, Fayzan Khan, Hyunjun Yi, Atharv Jha, Vihaan Vajpeyi, Ishaan Chandupatla, Madhav Nagpal

item.title: A recurrence in logarithmic M\"obius sums with coprimality conditions via Euler--Maclaurin
item.description: arXiv:2610.17720v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive a recurrence for logarithmically weighted M\"obius sums by combining M\"obius inversion with the Euler-Maclaurin summation formula. Consequently, starting from estimates of orders zero, one and two, we obtain polynomial approximations for these sums for every nonnegative integer exponent of $\log$. We then extend these estimates to sums with coprimality conditions via a convolution identity and to sums weighted by the reciprocal of the sum-of-divisors function. We also study the nonnegativity of the latter sums for every positive integer logarithmic order, establishing that they never change sign.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Zuniga Alterman

item.title: Mixed moment and joint non-vanishing of $\mathrm{GL}(3)\times\mathrm{GL}(1)$ and $\mathrm{GL}(1)$ $L$-functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.20792v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we study the mixed-moment problem for the product of central values of two $L$-functions twisted by a Dirichlet character of large conductor $q$. Precisely, for a fixed $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ Hecke-Maass cusp form $\pi$, we asymptotically evaluate the first moment, with $\textit{power-saving}$ error term for the product of central $L$-values $L(1/2, \pi\times\chi)\overline{L(1/2, \chi)}$ averaged over the $\textit{full family}$ $\{\chi\,(\mathrm{mod}\,{q}): Q\leq q\leq 2Q\}$ of primitive Dirichlet characters modulo $q$. And as a consequence, we also established the simultaneous non-vanishing of the aforementioned central $L$-values.
item.dc:creator: Sayan Ghosh, Pratim Mitra

item.title: Smoothness of Shortest Isogenies to Frobenius Conjugates
item.description: arXiv:2610.21488v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $E$ be chosen uniformly from the geometric isomorphism classes of supersingular elliptic curves over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ and $\delta_E$ be the minimum degree of isogenies from $E$ to its Frobenius conjugate $E^{(p)}$. We establish bounds for the smoothness probability of $\delta_E$ and hence affirm Wesolowski's $p^{1/3+o(1)}$ attack on the supersingular endomorphism ring problem is unconditional. We also establish a uniform asymptotic formula, with a main term expressed in terms of Dirichlet $L$ values, for the probability that a connection isogeny of degree $n$ exists between $E$ and $E^{(p)}$.
item.dc:creator: Yi Ouyang, Wei Wei, Zheng Xu

item.title: Classification of vanishing fusion rings of rank four
item.description: arXiv:2610.22000v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A fusion ring is said to be vanishing if one of its multiplication matrices has determinant zero. We classify all vanishing fusion rings of rank four. We then provide a more explicit classification in the integral case, which leads to new consequences: there are infinitely many nonisomorphic simple integral vanishing fusion rings of rank four and no simple integral fusion ring of rank four is 1-Frobenius. We also classify all Burnside fusion rings of rank four.
item.dc:creator: Jingcheng Dong, Sebastien Palcoux, Arnaud Plessis

item.title: A Non-Split Motohashi Formula for Toric Periods over Number Fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.22728v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a non-split Motohashi formula for toric Eisenstein periods over an arbitrary number field $F$. For a quadratic extension $E/F$, we compare toric Fourier inversion for a product of two Eisenstein series with the $\mathrm{GL}_2/F$-spectral expansion of its Rankin--Selberg kernel. The kernel regularizes the product in a cone of absolute convergence. Eisenstein corrections and contour residues give the geometric and residual terms in the meromorphically continued identity. Suitable test data give twisted first- and second-moment formulas for the completed $L$-functions of everywhere unramified toric characters. Over general $F$ these provide an adelic counterpart of the moment formulas of Duke--Friedlander--Iwaniec that does not use the geometry of Heegner points. In the CM case, we prove the absolute nonvanishing proportion $4.9\times10^{-4}$ for every totally real base field and all sufficiently large CM discriminants, with the threshold depending on the base field and no restriction on the number of ramified primes. We incorporate inverse Euler factors at small ramified primes into the mollifier. Local unit-group tests control the resulting moments and remove the ramified Euler-factor loss.
item.dc:creator: Liyang Yang

item.title: The sum-product conjecture holds for fixed-field lattice product constructions
item.description: arXiv:2610.26737v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study fixed-field analogues of the lattice product construction recently used by Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut, and Zhelezov to disprove the sum-product conjecture over the real numbers. These sets are of the form $A_n = P_nG_n \subset F$, where $F$ is a fixed number field, $P_n$ can be rescaled to a set of algebraic integers whose conjugates are polynomially bounded in $|P_n \setminus \{0\}|$, and $G_n$ occupies a positive proportion of a bounded box of scale $Y_n$ in a fixed positive-rank multiplicative lattice. We prove that these fixed-field constructions satisfy the sum-product conjecture, $\max\{|A_n+A_n|, |A_nA_n|\} \ge |A_n|^{2-o(1)}$ as $|A_n| \to \infty$, with no restriction on the relative growth of the two factors. More strongly, any fixed power saving in the product set forces an asymptotically maximal sumset: there exists $C > 0$ such that, for each fixed $\delta \in (0,1]$, if $|A_nA_n| \le |A_n|^{2-\delta}$ for all sufficiently large $n$, then $Y_n \to \infty$ and $|A_n+A_n|/|A_n|^2 = 1/2 + O_\delta((\log Y_n)^C/Y_n)$. In particular, the additive-box times unit-box construction of Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut, and Zhelezov cannot produce sum-product counterexamples in any fixed totally real number field, at any relative scales. The proof combines a bound for factorizations of algebraic integers with a more general maximal-sumset theorem for coefficient sets whose nonzero-element ratios have small Weil height. The latter controls multiplication fibers and combines a lattice strip estimate with logarithmic separation derived from the theorems of Yu and Matveev.
item.dc:creator: Harrison Lemley, David Chew

item.title: Isolated zeros of the Riemann zeta function and zeros of linear combinations of Dirichlet $L$-functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.26841v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $0<\gamma_1\leq \gamma_2\leq \cdots$ be the ordinates of the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function in the upper half-plane, counted with multiplicity, and fix $c>0$. We say that a non-trivial zero $\rho_n=\beta_n+i\gamma_n$ is $c$-isolated if $\min(\gamma_{n+1}-\gamma_n, \gamma_n-\gamma_{n-1})>2\pi c/\log \gamma_n$. Note that any isolated zero is necessarily simple and on the critical line. We prove unconditionally that there exists a positive constant $c>0$ such that at least $13/20$ of the zeta zeros are $c$-isolated. Moreover, we can show that this proportion is more than $1/2$ when $c=1/6$. Previously, it was not known unconditionally that there are infinitely many isolated zeros. We also show that there are positive proportions of $k$ consecutive ``moderate'' gaps (gaps larger than a constant times the average local gap) between the ordinates of the zeta zeros, for $k=3, 4, 5$. As an application we combine our work on isolated zeros (which we extend to Dirichlet $L$-functions) with an unconditional refinement of the Bombieri--Hejhal method to show unconditionally that at least $31\%$ of the zeros of a linear combination of two distinct primitive Dirichlet $L$-functions with the same conductor and parity lie on the critical line and have odd multiplicity. The previous unconditional record for this proportion was $7.38\times 10^{-9}$, which was obtained by Dousselin who refined and made explicit a result of Selberg.
item.dc:creator: Youness Lamzouri

item.title: On the Open Problem in the 2023 Simon Marais Mathematics Competition
item.description: arXiv:2610.30658v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that, for $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ not a perfect square, the only pairs of positive integers $\{a, b\}$ for which there exists $r \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $r^a + \sqrt{n}$ and $r^b + \sqrt{n}$ are both rational numbers are those of the form $\{a, a\}$ or $\{g, 2g\}$ (with $g$ odd). This resolves an open question presented in the 2023 Simon Marais Mathematics Competition.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Pisani

item.title: Low Genus Curves on Compact Shimura Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2502.11582v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate and compare the behaviors of complex curves on two major types of compact Shimura surfaces: compact variants of Picard and Hilbert modular surfaces. They are quotients of complex hyperbolic balls corresponding to moduli problems for abelian varieties with certain endomorphism types. We prove that if we fix a genus bound, then when the defining discriminant is large enough, low genus curves on the compact variant of Picard modular surfaces do not exist, while low genus curves may persist on the compact variant of Hilbert modular surfaces only if they are special curves, which parametrize those with extra endomorphisms. These results are special cases of a complex function field analogue of uniform boundedness on endomorphism types of abelian varieties. The proof requires understanding the repulsion of special subvarieties and relies on volume estimates in hyperbolic geometry.
item.dc:creator: Zhehao Li

item.title: Decomposition Theorem for Perfectoid Rings along General Ideals
item.description: arXiv:2606.06241v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using Andr\'e's lemma and the excision square for perfectoidization coming from $p$-complete arc descent, we prove new structural results about perfectoid rings and perfectoidization. The main result is a tameness theorem for torsion in perfectoid rings: if $R$ is a perfectoid ring and $I\subset R$ is an ideal, then the $I$-torsion in $R$ is $I_{\mathrm{perfd}}$-almost zero. This yields an excision-type decomposition of $R$ along its $I$-torsion part. We also study (semi)perfectoid rings and perfectoid ideals and take the opportunity to make some structural remarks about them.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Ishizuka, L\'eo Navarro Chafloque

item.title: On Perfectoidization of Finite Algebras over a Perfectoid Ring
item.description: arXiv:2606.12229v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study general properties of the perfectoidization of finite algebras over a perfectoid ring, which helps to understand some precise and explicit descriptions. For example, we prove that if $A=R[t]/(m(t))$ where $m(t)$ is monic, $R$ is perfectoid and the discriminant $d$ of $m(t)$ is a non-zero divisor of $R$ satisfying a bounded torsion condition, then $dA_{\mathrm{pfd}}\subset A$. We also prove a density criterion reducing the construction of the perfectoidization to adjoining suitable $p$-power roots modulo $p$. In the second part of the paper, we compute perfectoidizations in several families of examples, including Kummer-type extensions and split finite algebras.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Ishizuka, L\'eo Navarro Chafloque

item.title: On The Spectral Properties of Discrete Landscape Functions
item.description: arXiv:2608.11372v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the landscape function on a discretized interval. The discrete landscape has an explicit closed form, and its spectral coefficients can be computed exactly. We show that these coefficients lie in explicit abelian extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$ and obtain the bound $$[\mathbb{Q}(c_k(N)):\mathbb{Q}]\leq\varphi(N)$$ for every odd $k$. The Chandra--Jain conjecture, asserting that $[\mathbb{Q}(c_1(N)):\mathbb{Q}]=\varphi(N)$ for all $N\geq3$, has since been proved by Q. Zhou (Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.21935814). We then reduce higher modes to the coprime case. Exact computations for all 624 pairs with $3\leq N\leq50$ reveal only the degrees $\varphi(N/d)$ and $2\varphi(N/d)$ for non-coprime modes, where $d=\gcd(N,k)$. This motivates the Second Chandra--Jain Conjecture that this degree dichotomy holds generally. We also discuss connections with parity, the Arnold cat map, and Lefschetz numbers.
item.dc:creator: Aryaman Chandra, S. R. Jain

item.title: $p$-adic spectral zeta functions via the inverse Stieltjes transform
item.description: arXiv:2609.33660v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Spectral zeta functions provide a standard tool for regularizing determinants of differential operators in quantum physics. In a previous paper (J. Math. Phys. 66: 083505, 2025), we introduced a $p$-adic spectral zeta function for discrete spectra via a locally analytic interpolation function. In this paper we extend the framework to continuous spectra using the inverse Stieltjes transform. Starting from the resolvent of a bounded operator, we construct a generalized distribution, called the $p$-adic spectral distribution, and define bosonic and fermionic zeta functions and functional determinants. We establish their analytic properties, special value formulas, and Stirling expansions, and show that our previous framework is embedded into the present one in the discrete case. In this approach, the bosonic and fermionic cases exhibit an interesting symmetry. As an application, we consider the position operator in $p$-adic quantum mechanics on an arbitrary compact subset of $\mathbb{C}_{p}$.
item.dc:creator: Su Hu, Min-Soo Kim

item.title: Intersecting integer partitions: star bounds and counterexamples at every scale
item.description: arXiv:2610.01747v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Two integer partitions $t$-intersect if they have at least $t$ common parts, counted with multiplicity. We study the largest $t$-intersecting families of integer partitions of $n$ into exactly $k$ positive parts. The canonical $t$-star consists of the partitions containing at least $t$ ones. Applying Kupavskii's weak-spread theorem, we prove that this star is largest whenever $n\ge Ak^3$, for every fixed $A>24$ and all sufficiently large $k$, uniformly over $1\le t<k$. We also give counterexamples to Borg's conjecture at every intersection scale: for all sufficiently large $k$ and for every $1\le t\le \lceil k/4\rceil$, we describe $t$-intersecting families on integer partitions of $n=\lfloor tk^2/3\rfloor$ into $k$ parts which are strictly larger than the corresponding canonical stars. Moreover we present a family of counterexamples to Borg's conjectures about largest $t$-intersecting families of integer partitions of $n$ without restricting the number of parts.
item.dc:creator: Yury Person, Thomas Schweser

item.title: Beta-shifts without typical periodic optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.03619v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that beta-shifts whose lexicographically largest point is a Sturmian sequence do not have typical periodic optimization (TPO): on each such beta-shift there is a non-empty open set of Lipschitz functions whose unique maximizing measure is the Sturmian measure, which is not supported on a periodic orbit. These are the first known examples of beta-shifts without TPO, and, since they have the specification property, the first known examples of shift spaces with specification but without TPO. The corresponding beta-transformations do not have TPO in any space of H\"older functions on the interval. The main ingredient in the proofs is a rigidity property of Sturmian subshifts: modulo constants and Lipschitz coboundaries, the space of Lipschitz functions on such a subshift is one-dimensional. We also show that the set of $\beta>1$ for which the beta-shift or the beta-transformation does not have TPO is dense in $(1,\infty)$, but has zero packing dimension. The density is proved by a tuning construction, analogous to Douady--Hubbard tuning in the Mandelbrot set, which produces non-Sturmian subshifts with the same rigidity property. Finally, we show that every beta-shift has typical zero-entropy optimization: for an open dense set of Lipschitz functions, the maximizing measure is unique and its support has zero topological entropy.
item.dc:creator: Wen Huang, Oliver Jenkinson, Leiye Xu, Yiwei Zhang

item.title: On the structure of certain valued fields II
item.description: arXiv:2610.08395v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the structure of finitely ramified henselian valued fields of mixed characteristic with arbitrary residue fields via their residue rings of higher length, where a residue ring of length $n$ is the quotient ring of the valuation ring by the $n$-th power of its maximal ideal. We prove an approximate lifting theorem for homomorphisms between residue rings of higher length and explicitly determine the optimal bound of error of lifting. As applications, we obtain several Ax-Kochen-Ershov principles for relative completeness, relative existential completeness, and existential closedness using the pure ring structures on the residue rings. And we show that any formula on a residue ring of length $k$ is equivalent to a normal form of sentences in pure ordered group structure and special formulas at level $n$, uniformly for all finitely ramified henselian valued fields of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ and the same initial ramification index $e$. Here, for $n\ge k$, a special formula at level $n$ represents a definable set on a residue ring of length $k$ given by a projection image of a definable set in pure ring structure on a residue ring of length $n$. Also, such $n$ is optimally computed from the precise estimation of error of lifting and depends only on $k$, residue characteristic $p$, and initial ramification index $e$.
item.dc:creator: Junguk Lee, Wan Lee

item.title: A Simple Proof of I. Chowla's Theorem on Addition of Residue Classes
item.description: arXiv:2610.22427v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a brief, elementary proof of a striking theorem by I. Chowla on the addition of residue classes (1937) which generalizes the famous result of Cauchy and Davenport to residue classes modulo a composite.
item.dc:creator: Drew Duncan

item.title: Inverse Zero-Sum Problems of Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv constant: Property C and Property D conjectures
item.description: arXiv:2610.25271v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $C_n^r$ denote the direct sum of $r$ cyclic groups of order $n$, where $n\ge2$ and $r\ge1$. Properties C and D predict a uniform multiplicity structure for extremal zero-sum problems over $C_n^r$: every sequence of maximum length avoiding nonempty zero-sum subsequences of length at most $n$, or of length exactly $n$, respectively, should have the form $T^{n-1}$. We prove that, for every $r\ge4$ and every even $n\ge2$, each of these properties holds if and only if $n$ is a power of two. This gives negative answers to the general Property C problem posed by Gao, Hou, Schmid and Thangadurai Open Problems 1.2{GHST} in 2007, and disproves the Property D conjecture proposed by Gao and Geroldinger [Conjecture 7.2]{GG} in 2006.
item.dc:creator: Guoqing Wang, Xiangneng Zeng
